data.name: Muthukumar
data.gender_notes: Muthukumar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Muthu means 'God's grace'. Kumar means 'protector'. This name is derived from the ancient Indian scriptures and signifies the divine protection granted to an individual. The name Muthukumar carries the meaning “God's grace, protector” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Muthukumar usually hope their child will grow to embody god's grace, protector and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Muthukumar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's grace, protector.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muthukumar total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Muthukumar" is deeply rooted in the rich cultural traditions of Hinduism. In Hindu scriptures, Muthu is associated with sacred symbols represent divinity, such as the conch shell or the divine incarnation of Lord Vishnu, Muthuswami. The name conveys a sense of divine blessings and grace.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Muthukumar" lies in its deep connection to the belief that God's grace is the source of all protection and well-being. The Hindu tradition holds that God is the ultimate protector and provider, and the name Muthukumar is a reminder of this truth. By bearing this name, an individual is said to be constantly under God's watchful eye and beneficent protection.

historical_references.reference: Muthukumar was a renowned Tamil poet and scholar in the 16th century. He is best known for his work 'Thirumurugatruppadai' which is a commentary on the Tamil version of the 'Murugasubramaniya Upanishad'. This work is considered an important contribution to the Tamil literary tradition and is still widely studied and recited in South India.

Muthukumar was also a great saint and a prominent figure in the Shaivite tradition of Hinduism. He is believed to have lived in the 10th century and is known for his devotion to Lord Shiva. He composed several hymns in praise of Shiva and is regarded as an important spiritual figure in the Shaivite tradition.
